appearance_facts.fact: Vermont (VT) is filled with the darkest maroon color on the map, matching the low end of the legend scale.
Utah (UT) is filled with a very pale yellow/cream color, matching the high end of the legend scale.
Delaware (DE) is filled with a light yellow color, also near the high end of the legend scale.
Washington (WA) and South Dakota (SD) are also filled with the same darkest maroon color as Vermont.
New Mexico (NM), Indiana (IN), Mississippi (MS), and Tennessee (TN) are filled with a medium-to-dark red, indicating moderate risk.
Several states including California, Arizona, Colorado, Arkansas, and Alabama are filled with gray, indicating no data or a different category.
States like Texas, Florida, Georgia, and North Carolina are filled with orange or light orange, indicating moderate-to-high risk.
The legend is a vertical color bar ranging from dark maroon at the bottom to pale yellow at the top.

uncertain: The legend scale is inverted relative to typical 'high=red' conventions; here 'High' is labeled at the top (yellow, 100) and 'Low' at the bottom (maroon, 0).
The exact numerical risk index for Vermont, Utah, and Delaware is not printed on the map, only their relative color positions.
It is unclear if the gray states represent zero risk, missing data, or a different metric, though they are not options for selection.
